manifest.selection: All twenty published locate tasks from GiovanniGatti/cve-bench at commit 45cb1bf72f034eace43e46a9ae131c53a7fd292b, each adapted to its complete named Python module. Sources and corrections are pinned to the registered upstream fixing commit and vulnerable parent. No selection based on our model outcomes.

conditions.codex: Native Codex CLI, source-only configuration: full file in the prompt, JSON replacements, tools/web/host skills disabled, read-only process workspace, provider defaults for reasoning. This is not unrestricted default Codex.
conditions.vouch: Production Red review then Blue validation/repair, separate source workspaces, bounded file tools and skills, same model for both roles. Each role receives complete named files up to 256 KB in its initial context. Skill selection can publish a public plan in the same call. Progress is reported at decisions and context compaction, without a fixed cadence. Provider defaults for reasoning. No source execution or tool network access.

limitations: Source-only adaptation of CVE-Bench, not a replication of its runtime evaluation or leaderboard. Only the complete named module is provided, not the whole repository; some upstream corrections also change other modules. No original security tests, setup scripts, or application code are executed.

All twenty tasks are disclosed repair problems. Label agreement alone is not a useful detection score here; the primary displayed metric is named-module AST reference agreement. There are no fixed controls in this repair cohort.

Public historical patches may be in model training data. Repeated runs used to improve skills are development-set tuning, not held-out evidence. Every task, source, prompt, reference and grading rule stays fixed between repetitions.

Both conditions receive the complete named module and the same locate scope. Two pairs run concurrently with an equal eight-minute wall allowance. The role structure and number of model requests differ, so equal model and wall time do not mean equal compute.
Label agreement requires a verbatim source citation; the explanation still needs human review. Fixed controls are fixed only for the scoped concern, not certified free of all vulnerabilities.

AST equality is a conservative comparison with the registered reference correction. It can reject valid alternative fixes and is not a semantic or runtime regression test. Neither candidate nor reference code is executed.
All planned trials remain in the denominator. Errors and uncertain answers earn no credit. No target uplift, best-of selection, or removal of unsuccessful trials.

trials.summary: _load_data derives a filesystem path directly from the externally influenced CMap name and then deserializes the selected file with pickle. A name containing path separators can escape a configured CMap directory and select an unintended gzip-compressed pickle, potentially causing arbitrary code execution during deserialization. Rejecting names that are not plain basenames is the smallest source correction while preserving loading of normal CMap names. Exploitability still depends on whether an attacker can influence the name and place or reference a suitable file in the deployment, which is outside this snapshot.

The original function allowed absolute or parent-relative CMap names to escape configured directories before pickle deserialization. The candidate now rejects NUL-containing and non-basename names; exploitability still depends on external callers and filesystem contents, and no tests were run.

The localhost exemption uses a prefix comparison against the full network location, so an HTTPS host such as 127.0.0.1.example can be misclassified as localhost and have certificate verification disabled. Comparing the parsed hostname exactly preserves the intended localhost exception. Supporting deployment context is unavailable, but the defect is directly established by the supplied source.

The original function used prefix matching on the full netloc, allowing non-local HTTPS hosts beginning with the loopback string to disable certificate verification. The candidate minimally changes this to exact parsed-hostname equality. No tests or runtime checks were run; deployment reachability remains unknown.

File.__init__ derives _file_base directly from the untrusted uploaded filename without removing directory components. When UPLOAD_DIR and UPLOAD_KEEP_FILENAME are enabled, that value is later joined to the upload directory, allowing path traversal or absolute-path override. Applying os.path.basename to the split base is the smallest source correction. Exploitability depends on deployment configuration and any validation outside this snapshot.

File.__init__ originally preserved directory components from the supplied filename; filename-retention mode later uses that derived base in a writable path. The minimal candidate now applies os.path.basename before splitting. Exposure depends on external configuration, platform path semantics, and filesystem permissions; tests were not run.

The netrc command interpolates netrc_machine into a shell command and executes it with shell=True, permitting shell-command injection if that machine name is attacker-influenced. Parse the configured command before substituting the machine name, then execute the resulting argument vector without a shell. The exact Popen wrapper contract and callers are outside the supplied module, so compatibility cannot be fully verified source-only.

The original function interpolated netrc_machine directly into a command executed with shell=True, allowing shell interpretation rather than treating the value solely as data. The candidate minimally quotes the substituted value with shlex.quote; tests were not run, and caller control plus platform behavior remain uncertain outside this snapshot.

Export.normalize inserts strings and sequence elements into SQL single-quoted literals without escaping apostrophes, allowing supplied values to terminate the literal and alter the generated INSERT statement. Escape embedded apostrophes by doubling them, preserving existing output behavior otherwise. This source-only correction assumes ordinary PostgreSQL string-literal handling; broader parameterization and separately interpolated identifiers are outside the named concern, and deployment settings are unavailable.

Export.normalize manually quoted string-derived values without escaping, and export concatenated those fragments into an executed INSERT. The candidate replaces manual quoting with psycopg literal adaptation; the inspected diff changes only the named module, but tests were not run and runtime reachability is unknown.

KeyCache constructs several SQLite statements by interpolating issuer and key_id values directly into SQL, allowing SQL injection through externally influenced identifiers. The smallest correction is to parameterize those statements while preserving query behavior. Supporting input-validation and deployment context are outside this snapshot, so exploitability at each caller boundary remains uncertain.

KeyCache directly interpolated issuer and key_id values into SQLite statements, allowing those values to alter query syntax. The candidate correction replaces all affected SELECT, INSERT, and DELETE formatting with bound parameters. External callers, deployment state, and runtime behavior were unavailable, and no tests were executed.

Auth0OAuthenticator defaults the account identity to the user's email but does not require Auth0's email_verified claim before delegating authorization. An unverified email could therefore be treated as an established identity. The smallest correction rejects missing or false email_verified values, then preserves the base authenticator's authorization behavior. Supporting modules and deployment configuration are unavailable, so this conclusion assumes the documented auth0_user state contains the Auth0 user-info claims.

The original class uses Auth0 email as the default principal but had no provider-specific authorization check for verified email. The candidate adds a fail-closed email_verified gate before delegating to inherited authorization; base-hook compatibility and runtime behavior remain unverified because supporting modules and tests are unavailable.

Table names read from an externally supplied SQLite schema are interpolated directly into PRAGMA and SELECT statements. A crafted database can therefore alter the generated SQL. Quote each table name as a SQLite identifier before use. Call-site trust and deployment controls are unavailable in this source-only snapshot.

The original function interpolates database-controlled table names into SQL without identifier escaping, allowing crafted schema identifiers to alter SQL parsing. The candidate minimally escapes embedded double quotes and uses double-quoted identifiers in both statements. Caller reachability and runtime impact are outside this snapshot; no tests were run.

The method passes externally derived logging configuration directly to logging.config.dictConfig(). Python dictConfig treats a "()" entry as a callable factory, so an untrusted configuration can request execution of an imported callable. Rejecting that directive recursively is the smallest source-local correction. The snapshot does not establish whether configuration files and KEDRO_LOGGING_CONFIG are restricted to trusted users, so practical exposure remains deployment-dependent.

The original method forwarded logging_config directly to dictConfig without runtime type or dynamic-factory validation. A narrow pre-call guard was added; runtime behavior remains unverified because supporting modules, deployment state, and executed tests are unavailable.

The function incorrectly exempts all requests with Sec-Fetch-Mode: no-cors. Such requests can still be cookie-authenticated and state-changing, so only the existing token-authenticated, WebSocket, and safe navigation cases should bypass XSRF validation. Supporting handler and deployment behavior is outside the snapshot, but the exemption is unsafe from the supplied function alone.

The original function unconditionally exempted Sec-Fetch-Mode "no-cors" requests from XSRF validation regardless of HTTP method. The candidate removes only that exemption and its stale comment reference. Supporting callers, deployment behavior, and runtime tests were unavailable.

The check compares each option before removing leading whitespace. If downstream option parsing normalises or tokenises that whitespace, an unsafe option can evade this guard. The smallest source correction is to left-strip each option before the existing comparisons. Whether all callers subsequently parse such strings cannot be confirmed from this single-module snapshot.

The original method normalized configured unsafe names with lstrip("-") but did not normalize candidate options equivalently, leaving alternate leading-hyphen forms outside the intended prefix check. The candidate now normalizes each option before comparing it with bare_option. Tests were not run, and supporting modules and deployment behavior are outside the snapshot.

read_prev_trailer recursively follows attacker-controlled /Prev offsets without tracking previously visited xref sections, so a cyclic trailer chain can cause unbounded recursion. The smallest source-only correction carries a visited-offset set through the recursion and rejects repeats; integration behavior outside this module is unverified because supporting modules and deployment state were not provided.

The original method recursively followed /Prev offsets without tracking repeats, so cyclic chains were not deliberately rejected. A localized visited-offset guard was added; tests and runtime checks were not run, and supporting modules and deployment state remain outside scope.

dirpath is concatenated directly with the configured data directory, allowing unresolved parent components or absolute-style input to select paths outside that directory. Resolve both paths and reject any result not contained by the data root. Caller-side validation and deployment behavior are outside this snapshot.

The original method overwrote its joined path with unchecked concatenation, then used that path for filesystem access without canonicalization or root-containment validation. The candidate now resolves canonical root-relative paths and rejects paths outside the configured data root. Caller reachability, deployment permissions, and runtime behavior remain unverified; no tests were run.

MultipartParser accepts an unbounded number of part headers and places no per-header limit on field or value length when max_size is left at its unbounded default. Add configurable finite limits for header count and individual header field/value size. Supporting configuration and compatibility expectations outside this module are unavailable, so the proposed defaults are conservative.

Original MultipartParser had only an unbounded-by-default whole-body limit and no dedicated header byte or count limits. The candidate adds per-part limits of 64 KiB aggregate header bytes and 100 headers, raising MultipartParseError when exceeded. Diff inspection passed protected-file checks; tests were not run, and external deployment limits remain unknown.

get_template uses the unnormalised URI as a cache key and joins its leading-slash-stripped value to each template directory.
